items.headline: Meta releases Muse Wonder, its first frontier-class AI model
items.summary: Meta's Superintelligence Lab launched Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full, its most capable models yet, after years of trailing OpenAI, Anthropic and Google on frontier benchmarks. The closed-weight models break from Meta's earlier open Llama strategy and emphasize long-running coding and agent tasks.

items.headline: FBI arrests OpenAI employee over hidden recording device in conference room
items.summary: A 35-year-old OpenAI engineer was charged after a listening device, concealed in toilet paper and plugged into a TV's USB port, was found in an executive conference room. OpenAI said it saw no evidence the employee accessed model weights, source code or customer data, and has terminated him.

items.headline: Character.AI files for Chapter 11 bankruptcy as Disney moves to hire most of its staff
items.summary: The chatbot company filed for Chapter 11 in Delaware, and Disney has offered jobs to 66 of its roughly 86 employees as part of a $20 million stalking-horse bid for a license to its technology. The deal underscores how quickly consumer AI-companion startups have struggled financially even as demand for their products grew.

items.headline: Nvidia in advanced talks to acquire Hugging Face for about $12.9 billion
items.summary: The Information reported Nvidia has agreed to buy the open-source AI platform, while Reuters, citing Business Insider, described the talks as advanced but not yet a signed deal. It would be one of Nvidia's largest acquisitions as it pushes further into the AI software layer.

items.headline: Rivian says its vehicles will eventually run third-party AI agents
items.summary: Rivian CEO RJ Scaringe said at TechCrunch Disrupt that future vehicles could run AI agents built by outside companies, including Anthropic, beyond the automaker's current in-house voice assistant. It signals automakers increasingly see cars as a new platform for third-party AI agents.

items.headline: Anthropic releases Claude Opus 5.5, a cheaper flagship coding and agent model
items.summary: Anthropic's new flagship runs roughly 20-40% cheaper than Opus 5 while performing close to its larger Claude Fable 5.1 model on most tasks, with external evaluators including METR reviewing its safety behavior. It's aimed squarely at coding, agent workflows and enterprise analytics.

items.headline: Amazon triples Nvidia GPU commitment to about 3 million chips for AWS
items.summary: Nvidia disclosed on an earnings call that Amazon expanded an earlier order to roughly 3 million Blackwell Ultra, Rubin and Rubin Ultra GPUs for AWS data centers, citing demand from AI labs, enterprises and governments that has outrun forecasts. The deal also covers Nvidia networking, CPUs and robotics software.

items.headline: Big Tech plans record $680 billion in AI infrastructure spending for 2026
items.summary: Alphabet, Amazon, Meta and Microsoft collectively plan to spend a record $680 billion this year on AI data centers and networking, with Alphabet alone raising its capex guidance to $180-190 billion. Investors have pushed back on some of the hyperscalers, demanding clearer proof the spending will pay off.
